title: I think that in this community and similar ones we sugarcoat reality
author: PatientBeautiful7372
selftext:
Let me explain. I'm making a text simulator, kind of like The Sims. 

I've shown it to AI fanatics (for lack of a better term) and to people who played The Sims/Paralives/Bitlife/Inzoi but don't care about AI. 

I see potential in my game; I started it out of love. I don't intend to get rich from it.

The difference in opinions between the two is too overwhelming. 

People have told me it's fun to play in its current state. But only the player group has been able to give me constructive criticism. 

Here are some examples, though there have been way more: The family tree showed significant bugs; some things were visually confusing; there was an alert sound that sometimes played when it shouldn't; after three generations with the same family, the surname became corrupted and the balance of needs and economics.

Without those criticisms, the game would have progressed much less and I probably would have missed something.

That leads me to think that group one has praised me without playing it (it wouldn't be a problem in itself if it weren't for the fact that they said they had) or that the AI-loving community is incapable of giving constructive criticism because they don't want to admit that it's not perfect.

I have experience in video game development and storytelling, and I've used AI for coding, which is my weakest area. There are no AI-generated images (there are very few, but I created them myself using pixel art), nor are there any sounds.

comments.author: Nice_Try4389
comments.body:
I have likewise ran into issues with people in group one and I think overwhelmingly the difference is they see AI not as a tool but as a straight up replacement for everything.  All they care about is good enough.  When it comes to say music all they care is that is sounds close enough to what they like, and put no real thought or effort into the listening, for them it is just background.  Similarly when it comes to art they just care that it looks pretty and nice, but the actual quality they could care less about.  Meanwhile YOU see it more as a tool and you care about the result of the output and making sure it is something of genuine quality and not just “good enough”, similarly the regular gamers you shared it with are of the same bent.  They want to play something quality that they can enjoy and connect with not just something that passes the time.

To me it is the difference between an asset flip game and something that Phantasmaphobia.  Both use 100% licensed assets from the unity or Unreal store.  The difference is the makers of Phantasmaphobia make the effort to hand pick the assets to use and frame them in such a way so all of them serve the game rather than just cranking something out.  And I think that is the difference you are seeing both with the groups and how you yourself relate to each.  You yourself are first and foremost concerned about making sure everything is in service of the game itself, rather than just wanting to make a game.

Sorry for the long winded explanation.

replies.author: PatientBeautiful7372
replies.body:
I agree with you.

It was sad to find that they don't care about what they made, but that it was made with AI. They didn't take my feedback well either, even if it was with good intentions.

comments.author: shimroot
comments.body: And this is why when you build a product (regardless of type) you should talk with the target audience, not with just anyone. Only the target audience will give meaningful feedback since they are (potentially) the ones that are most invested in your product succeeding.

comments.author: gadimus
comments.body: The one major downside of our current era is that people have so many things competing for their time. In order to get legitimate feedback you need to build something exceptional OR start with a community first, one that loves your work, and then build. Otherwise it's hard to compete with the noise out there.

comments.author: Electrical-Cloud4141
comments.body: I see the same thing happen to games made with AI art. There is an AI enthusiast group that will say anything made with AI looks good, and they will tell a dev that anyone who thinks it looks bad just hates AI. When in fact it looks terrible, uncanny, or sticks out like a sore thumb because the assets do not match each other in style.

replies.author: Live_Fall3452
replies.body: To be honest, everything I’ve seen on Reddit suggests the opposite is more prolific - people will go out of their way to attack games that use any AI at all, regardless of how, without even taking a serious look or trying it.

replies.author: PatientBeautiful7372
replies.body: I know. That's why I was reluctant of using it. There's a specific group of AI enthusiast that I don't want to be associated with, but it's not something very popular to say here.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
This isn't any different or unique to AI.

Its the same trap most amateur creatives run into.  Their playtesters/feedback group ends up being their friends and fans, so of course theres inherent bias that skews the results.  If you want real feedback you need to pay for it.  Same as it ever was.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
don't think its an ai / community issue and more of a people issue . its like that 10 page report you gave your boss with page 6 you wrote a sentence saying he's an asshole and eats shit for dinner. You ask if he read the entire thing and he said yes with a smug grin...you keep your job and even get promoted , clearly he didn't read that shit as he said. 

And as a person below pointed out target audience / focus groups , talking to fellow builders u either gonna get glazed / ignored / set on fire . Also did you not see the bugs before giving it to others.

replies.author: PatientBeautiful7372
replies.body:
Not all. Even the computer specifications or windows version can alter that. Also I have a Linux version and a Windows version. I just have one person giving me feedback about the Linux version unfortunately.
As for the bugs mention it's harder when you've seen the game too many times and know where is everything. The same goes to "creative thinking". I try to think about breaking (marrying, divorcing, having many kids, being fired, etc) but my imagination has a limit and more people means more ways to break it.

comments.author: Henjineer
comments.body: A group of people who are all too eager to offload any cognitive tasks aren't good at providing nuanced, constructive feedback? Gee golly gosh, color me surprised.

replies.author: PatientBeautiful7372
replies.body: I'm more disappointed than surprised LoL. It was a little of a rant.

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: spectralfew
comments.body: Criticism is vital. You won’t improve by thinking your work is awesome all the time. Group one isn’t one whose input I’ll ever seek, and I’ve observed what you’re referring to here.

replies.author: PatientBeautiful7372
replies.body: Yeah that's my point. There always good comments and little constructive criticism.

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body: It's hard to be critical tho to be fair :) I pointed something out about someone's game the other day here and still feel kinda bad about it.

comments.author: chmillout
comments.body: Guys I see 10% of actual game work on this sub and 90% of random AI ranting, can we just focus on creating games finally?

comments.author: EternalDreamIP
comments.body:
The problem is not AI, is workflow. And the only thing any dev sould know and accept is that QA is the 99% of the job. 
If QA is not there, the game is to be a compilation of bugs and glitches. It's not AI's fault. It's been always like that. That's why companies spend more polishing the game, than creating it. QA is the top tier.

replies.author: PatientBeautiful7372
replies.body: I agree. AI enthusiast are terrible with QA in my experience.

replies.author: EternalDreamIP
replies.body: Tbh, game devs too. In my experience at least (more than 15 years in the area). AI is just letting more people try to create things, and most of them are new to this because it was too far from their possibilities before AI. Let's see what happens in 2-3 years.

comments.author: NewOwlllll
comments.body: The three-generation surname bug is the giveaway. Anyone who genuinely played that far would've hit it, so next time just ask what happens to the surname. That instantly filters out the ones who lied about playing.

comments.author: ResenhaDoBar
comments.body: You have to listen to players for feedback, dev feedback is usually biased, players only care about the game itself

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
I see this in all AI subs. It's the difference between people who already have the skills using AI and people who don't using AI. 

The people who could already do something before AI just have a lot higher standard for it replacing their  skills.

That's basically why there's so much slop content. People that are now creating things using AI that didn't have any of the skills required to do it before AI, generally just have a lot lower standards for what they think is good.

If someone can't do something without AI the AI getting them even 50% there is seen as good enough.
